title: Good quality set of headphones
text:
I've tried several different types of inexpensive-mid range headphones and these are by far my favorite out of all the ones that I've tried. Maybe more importantly though is not that they are "better than other headphones" but rather that as that a stand-alone product they are actually really good. They are made from good quality materials and have a good sound. This is one product that I felt like actually came and looks pretty much exactly like the picture in the product description. They are designed with cushion pretty much everywhere, so your head doesn't get pinched in weird ways that make it hurt. The earpieces (earmuffs?) are comfortable and isolate the sound pretty well. Both what you're listening to from those around you as well as the ambient noise that might bother/distract you. They fold up for storage, and fold up smoothly. Like I said before, I'm impressed. I always try to think of cons and here are my biggest three:

1.) The cable isn't detachable. It's plenty long which gives you a lot of freedom but I wish it were detachable
2.) The color is super bright. I like it a lot most of the time. . . but it definitely makes you stand out which isn't always what I'm going for.
3.) The sound is good but not so good that it blows you away

Overall I really like them and assuming that they continue to work I will definitely continue to recommend them.
I was fortunate enough to be able to review these and get a discount on the price but I give them 5 stars because I am super happy with them and think that they deserve them. I definitely don't give everything 5 stars.

title: Unbelievable! Chi-Fi delivering overtime with these
text:
Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome

title: Audiophile quality at a budget price!
text:
I have two issues, and it is not with the IEM's themselves, but the company that sold them. First, the ones I purchased were originally returned. How do I know? Because whoever had them before me had worn them, and left ear wax on the silicone ear pieces. Luckily, they were not the size I wear so I made sure to wash all of the ones that came with the IEM's (included the dirty ones). And second, they went on sale two days after I bought them so I had to send an email to the seller to see if I can get the $10.00 off. UPDATE: 6/8/22 - Got the $10.00 discount!!

Other than those two things, they are excellent IEM's! If you look at the frequency response of these, and realized that they are tuned, they're great for someone in the mid 50's. As you get older, you notice that your hearing loses higher frequencies. Pretty much every frequency above 12kHz are gone. These are tuned perfectly for someone who has lost those frequencies, and these start dropping off after 10kHz. So if you are younger, adjust the treble if you need to.

How good are they? If you have ever heard Bruce Hornsby & The Range's song "Every Little Kiss," you can hear Bruce shift his weight on the bench while playing his Steinway at the beginning of the song.

So, if you love listening to music, and don't feel like forking hundreds of dollars for earbuds, these are the ones to buy. Oh, and the bass is excellent!!

title: Very good for the money.
text:
I grabbed these for quick field recordings with some zoom equipment. I wanted something smaller that wouldn't take up half my case when I was basically just checking to see that things weren't clipping anyway.

I have nothing but good things to say about these. I have used ones that were a few hundred dollars and these are very similar.

I do not have the mic version, so I can't speak to the quality of the mic.

These DO NOT HAVE ACTIVE NOICE CANCELLING. I am so sick of that term getting confused with items that are noise isolating just by virtue of having a good fit. These do a great job of blocking sound, but if you are expecting noise cancellation you will be disappointed.

The manual is ridiculous. It looks like it was translated in google translator. Things don't make sense at all if you don't already know what the paragraph is probably talking about. Fortunately these are basically plug and play. You insert the wires (there are pictures showing how, so it doesn't matter how poorly translated it is) and off you go.

title: Great budget IEM
text:
So I'll ride the hype train on this one. These sound very good. They have excellent clarity. Imaging and separation is good, soundstage is... well fairly small. But for $50 these may be the best I've experienced.

In terms of audiophile quality, these do beat the Tinhifi T2's (also same price range); from the perspective of fidelity of sound. The Tinhifi T2 is a very enjoyable headphone - it is just 'rounded off' and more Harman tuned.

Pros:
Clarity and detail are great for this price range.
Imaging and separation are good for the price range.

Neutral:
Despite me saying these are more true to sound than the T2, these are V shaped. The low end is pronounced/punchy, and the upper end is pronounced. This can be good or bad depending on your taste.

Cons:
I am new to the audiophile hobby, so I couldn't point to an exact frequency range, but the treble definitely spikes at one or more frequency. This is largely eliminated by using foam tips. But these treble spikes can make this IEM fatiguing, especially with certain tracks, and especially when you stick with the stock silicone tips.

Overall:
Great IEM for the price, I do not regret buying them. Their quality is excellent. And I even joy the build quality on these. The cable that came with it is... okay... It's one of those clear plasticy rubbery jobs that feels like it should be on a pink set of a 5 year old girl's headphones. But they do the job.

title: Works great for electronic drums, but you'll NEED foam tips.
text: I purchased these in July of 2019 and have been using them as IEM's almost daily for rehearsal, live gigs and playing at church, all on Roland V-Drums. The sound is fantastic. I got these as an upgrade from the KZ AS10s. The AS10s didn't have the low end I needed playing the V-Drums, but the ZS10 Pro's have enough. Not booming, thumping low end, but enough low end to not need to spend any more money on "better" IEM's. I used the foam tips for a while and that improved the sound and fit, but found the ZS10 Pro still didn't have as good of isolation as the AS10's. I also got the upgraded cable and could not be happier. No tangling at all. After 1 year, these still work perfectly and have never had any issues. None. If you want super-sub bass freq's, then these probably aren't for you. But if you want killer sound for under $50, these are it.

text:
This is an excellent product that could have been improved by optional noise cancellation.

I cannot complain about the latter, because it is not a feature of the unit and it is not specified as one. I just think it would be great on the plane or bus when I travel.

Other than that, the microphone and headset are great. The noise level is low on the microphone, so I can talk over it easily. The only issue I have is noise in the background when in a noisy environment. And that is not the fault of the headset, but the lack of a feature.

The headset independent of that limitation is amazing. The sound is the best I have ever heard on earbuds. The bass is astounding. The clarity is as well. The microphone works wonderfully in almost all situations except truly excessive background noise.

However, the most astounding aspect is the bluetooth is flawless. I have not found a situation in which I could not receive a clear signal and clear sound. It may be impacted by background noise, but it is never the wireless connection.

These sound better than some over the ear headsets I have. Quality, feel, fit, etc. are all fantastic.

Noise reduction is required for environments that are not background friendly. If you are more interested in listening to music and conducting wireless chat in a controlled environment or at least one not exposed to extreme background noise, these are the ticket.

text:
I thought "They're cheap, why not?" I expected that Sony would at least make a semi-descent product, but I was wrong. They only cut out about 5% of ambient noise. I tested them in a lot of different environments and it didn't perform well under any circumstance.

I compared them to a pair of low-end headphones ($20) to set a baseline, see below.

Test:
In flight - no noticeable difference between each pair
While driving - slightly better muffling of midrange noise, but slight (2% better)
Fan on high & low - slightly better canceling of low freq noise (2% better)
In crowed auditorium - slight better muffling (1% better)

They barely did any better than the cheap-o, non-noisecanceling, over the ear headphones I got for half the price.

The biggest thing I noticed is that the very little amount of noise that was actively cancelled was replaced fully by a hissing sound. This made the headset pretty much useless.

I would recommend not buying these headphones. I returned the set I bought, and got my money back. There are better headsets at this price.

title: I'm returning these.
text:
I've been looking for NC headphones, and I have an overseas trip coming up. So when I saw these I did a rare thing and bought them from a local retailer without any prior research. I like Sony products. I have a 55" TV, blu-ray player, surround sound, and 5 disc changer - all Sony. I like them all. These headphones are a joke. On a prior overseas trip I tried the expensive Bose model of NC headphones, and was very impressed. I thought if these were a fraction as good, they would be worth it. Nope.

Pros: Rather comfortable for the ten minutes I wore them. Low price (assuming NC works - which it doesn't). Music sounded great with the NC switch on or off. Blocked a fair amount of noise just physically.

Cons: Falsely advertised as NC. The only noticeable difference with the switch on was a slight hiss. No carrying case included. Wires on both ear cups.

Eager to try them - I went outside where my neighbor two doors down was mowing the lawn. I noticed a fair amount of noise BLOCKING when I put on the headphones. When I flipped the switch I could hear the slight hiss i expected - but the neighbor's mower was not attenuated whatsoever. If I could plainly hear a distant mower with these activated, how could I expect them to attenuate the sounds within a passenger jet? Granted the sound these produced was great for dub-step - my test of dynamic range. But good sound wasn't the point of these.

If you want noise cancelling, look elsewhere. If you just want good sounding headphones, you can probably do better for your money.

title: Pass on these.
text:
This is my third pair of Raycons via their website. I'm writing the review here to preserve the review.

My first pair was their E50s, which I really liked but the left randomly stopped charging. After contacting customer service and confirming all troubleshooting, they gave me a discount on another pair as I was out of warranty. I then got my first pair of Blue Fitness buds early September.

After they arrived, I felt the sound quality was great, loved the way they fit, awareness mode is a game changer, wonderful battery life, and they still worked independently which is a major need for me. Right away, I noticed some charging issues, occasionally they wouldn't charge in the case and I'd have to tap it gently a few times until the lights came on to indicate charging. No big deal since they charge quickly and it only occasionally happened, figured it was from carrying them in my pocket around the house. Then my earbuds would randomly disconnect, even when I was right next to my phone. Even had them power off without reason. Not to mention, the left earbud is meant to lower the volume and it only increased the volume. Then one day the left earbud randomly wouldn't sync to my phone, despite trying to factory reset multiple times. They'd turn on and off, but wouldn't attempt to pair to anything. I wrote in to customer service and they directed me to the link for replacement or exchange. I figured to give it one more chance before moving into another product.

This process was fairly simple. I was given a shipping label and the option to schedule as USPS too.

After receiving my new pair, I immediately put them on charge until it appeared fully charged. Paired them to my phone. They were only charged to 10%. Had to do the same gentle tap to get them to charge. This did get them to 100%, but only with careful monitoring when left on a flat surface. Same great qualities as the previous pair, but this charging issue happens every time I put them in the case. Today is my second or third day with the new pair, and I'm over it. I left them charging all day while I was out running errands to come home to them being 10% when I did the tap method to make sure they were charging before I left. For earbuds at $119, although I received them at 30% off, this is ridiculous. The great qualities mean NOTHING if they aren't functional.

title: Great WIRED headset!
text:
It's so good to find more wired TRRS headsets hitting the market. For a while it seemed like only wireless ones were selling and the wired models were all low-end earbud styles or the kind that have the mic embedded by your ears instead of your mouth.
This is a good over-the-ear style set, with decent bass response and sound quality, as well as a mic on the wire. I really like the placement of a microphone on the wire, it is second only to the telescoping mic style you see receptionists and gamers using. It keeps the mic relatively close to your mouth (rather than headsets that put the mic by your ears) so you pick up your voice more than ambient noise in the room. Just keep in mind, it is a TRRS set which means it has the extra pin on the plug for a mic. It may not work properly in standard TRS headphone plugs (stereo only, designed for use with headsets without a mic), although some can work with both.
Most modern laptops support TRRS, as well as tablets and phones (if you're lucky enough to still have a 3.5mm headset jack!).

I decided to take a gamble on these hook-on earbuds as they are similar in style to my MPOW Flame Lite buds which I use in the gym, but the MPOW brand is lacking in sound, so I gambled on these and WON!! These buds are INCREDIBLY LOUD and CLEAR. Two things I look for in earbuds. They pair easily enough as "F4" on bluetooth. Upon calling my bluetooth soundcheck friend, I had to turn the volume down to half as she came in loud and clear and she received no distortion from me. We managed a three hour phone converstation and the batteries were still going strong.

I later took the buds out to my patio for some music streaming and they passed the test of fidelity with flying colors. There is NO tinny sound on these earbuds and the bass comes through clear, not muddle or overpowering. I had to keep the volume at half, as the buds produce loud sound with no distortion. I even used the phone charger built into the case for a bit. Using the phone charger does drain the charge for the buds in the cradle so I would recommend using the phone charge in emergency situations mostly. All in all a GREAT set of buds that rival high-end mainstream competitors. I have over a dozen earbuds and headphones, and I can say with certainty that these are standouts and will definitely be replacing my MPOW buds in the gym. You can't go wrong with purchasing these earbuds.

title: Bass is controlled.  Tight even.  Treble's even better
text: I'm not used to IEMs.. I've always either used over-ear headphones (aiwas from 20 years ago, at least)  or other decent 10 dollar earbuds like JVC marshmallows or those panasonic ones which people like.  I'd always kind of thought that it was just a given with earbuds that they will either be drowned in bass/low mid frequencies or there will be none and instead strong midrangy grindy/uncomfortable frequencies -  I've played with a LOT of really bad earbuds.  I sort of just thought because everybody's ear canal shape is slightly different, you would just have to put up with varying degrees of uncontrolled bass.  Some cheap buds are better than others in this regard.  I found those two sets I mentioned earlier were pretty consistently okay in the bass, but it wasn't really until I tried these that I realized what I was missing in terms of clear, airy highs.. It really sets up the soundstage.  It's funny, because as a turntable user, you'd think that I would demand excellence in my portable music experience (I use a pretty high bitrate lossy compression), but I just always kinda wrote it off.  I'm really impressed with this pair.  They seem well built, sound really three dimensional.  They'd be good gaming headphones.  Though I bought them for digital media, I find myself grabbing them instead of my cans when i listen to lps in bed... The high transients sound really nice as long as the volume isn't too aggressive.  One caveat.. I don't listen to a ton of modern music.  The music I generally listen to for my own amusement requires a pretty flat eq envelope.  But I did throw some Gojira through them at some point and I still think they sounded less muddy than my other headphones.

title: Unbeatable at this price point and more than worth it, but may not last years for you
text:
How I use them:
Worship leader--I use them as in-ear monitors for rehearsals and on stage during live events.

Frequency of use:
Generally twice per week, occasionally more if we have multiple events, occasionally less if I get a week off.

My take:
I was honestly blown away by the sound quality at this price point. All the other five star reviews noting this are accurate. These are so impressive that they are the goto in-ears for any new member that comes on and needs a good pair fast. Some move on from them to more expensive brands, but more and more the members of our teams get these to start and then stick with them. I think mine is the first pair to suffer any kind of failure (but I was also the first to get them, so that makes sense).

The only real con is that after about 9 or so months of twice-weekly-ish use, the wire in the cable on the right ear (for shaping around the ear) popped through. My best guess is it's a quality control issue, as opposed to me just being hard on them, only because I keep them in a hard case when not in use, and almost never use the right ear, keeping it out so I can better hear the room sound. Only once in a blue moon do I use the right ear and then only for a minute or so to get through a difficult part where I need to block room sound and be hyper focused to get something right. After it pierced through the cable sheathing, I gently removed it to keep it from snagging or poking or just tearing up the cable from the inside since it wasn't seated in place anymore. A few weeks later, the right ear didn't work at all anymore. Left side is unaffected. So at some point, I'll get another pair and see if it's just the cable that needs replacing or if the right monitor just went bad and it's unrelated to the cable, but for now I'm going to try out another model of KZs because they all have fantastic reviews and I want to see if I can find something even better for me.

I do have relatively small ears, so these are a tad bulky, but all of them are for me. I'd need to get into the super pricey custom stuff to fix that, so these aren't faulted for that in my book. They're really great in-ears.

All in all, still 5 stars because for twenty bucks I got more than 6 months worth of two hundred dollar quality. But do be aware that they probably won't last forever.

title: CozyPhones are, in fact, pretty cozy.
text:
This sleep headphone band fits quite comfortably. Before I bought this I was introduced to the product at my mom's house and I wear a considerably bigger hat size than her, but the stretchy band fit both of us perfectly. Despite my big bobblehead of a noggin, I don't find this too tight even when worn for hours, and yet it hasn't become stretched out either. A smaller headed person could still wear mine. Also in regard to fit, the light weight, low profile speakers can easily be moved inside the headband to exactly where they are most comfortable and best heard for each wearer (I did have to move the speakers back when I tried my mom's). Once in place the speakers stay put really well simply due to the friction between the textures of the fuzzy fabric pad over each speaker and the headband's fabric. I occasionally have to tweak where a speaker is sitting as I put them on, but once in place the speaker has never needed to be repositioned during wear. I also love that the speakers can be slipped out through the back so the headband can be laundered.

I would say that the sound quality is that of average headphones. I don't notice a discernable difference between these and any other headphones I own, but I may not have as attuned an ear as some people seem to have, so my feelings won't be hurt if you get a second opinion on this part.

I don't really have any cons to mention for these, but wait, I almost forgot to mention that when buying these I saw multiple other reviewers warn that the dye bled from the colored edge of their headbands. I should say that I specifically bought the one with the white edge to avoid that happening. I've had no dye transfer at all from mine, so I can suggest getting the white edged band if that's a concern.

Hope this helps.

title: They Could Build in a Tiny Modicum of Durability
text:
Are you tired of lousy reviewers who write up glowing 5-star reviews after one week, so you have no idea if the thing lasts a year? Are you tired of paid reviewers who say "As advertised"? Or worse, "Arrived on time"? Be still, my wild heart! Here, take my money!
Like, why aren't they reviewing the Post Office for that?

Well, your help has arrived.

When these started failing, I searched my order history to see how long they lasted.
Slightly over a year!
I would pay more for more durability.
However, I did pay more once - a lot more. Before these, I bought a set of Sleepphones. Directly from the company, maybe before they were offered here.
I paid SEVERAL TIMES as much for those!
Warning: It does not buy you durability.

So I like these slightly better, because they are not so unconscionably exorbitant.

However: "Better Than Sleepphones" isn't saying much. It is a very, very low bar to clear.

So if I see ANYthing like these, that give you a few more durability units for a few more dollars, I'm on it.
Sadly, I expect to see the few more dollars charged, with nothing in return.

I still don't know whether to buy these again. The other depressing option is to buy the speaker "refill".
You know, the same junk that was installed in this headband?
There is a business opportunity for someone to make a durable, affordable set of thin speakers. Surprisingly, some excellent, affordable products are "Made in USA".

Do it!

title: Best Sleep Headphones I've Tried (Update at end of review)
text:
I fall asleep to audiobooks, and have tried a lot of speakers and headphones with mixed results. My husband bought me these AcousticSheep SleepPhones recently, and what a difference they make! They're very comfortable - okay, the mediums are a little large for me, but I've found a way to position them so they work perfectly. The speakers are thin and pliable, so they're comfortable even if you roll over and lie on them, and the sound is pleasant - not too boomy or too shrill, and you can move the headband so you can listen in both ears or only one, if you prefer.

The one catch is that the wires leading out of the headphones are pretty thin, and judging my previous experience using many headsets and speakers in bed, they're going to break inside at some point. Then I'll either have to order more or perhaps do a little creative wire work and attach new, stronger wires. I'd be perfectly happy to replace these once a year as they've improved my quality of sleep (I'm used to waking when I roll onto a hard plastic speaker or earphone).

BTW, the headband itself is sooo soft and comfy - none of the headbands I've used on my hair over the years are this cozy.

Like it said on the package, these truly are pajamas for your ears ;-)

***Update Feb 9, 2014***

It's been just short of a year since I write the above review. Since then, I ordered a second smaller pair of SleepPhones, the band of which wasn't as soft and furry, but it was good for wearing when doing housework. This one didn't come in the same packaging - the packaging was more minimual. My original pair of SleepPhones' wire on the left ear did indeed break, and I bought a third pair. This was in a much smaller package, but was furry and comfy as the first set. Hopefully it will last a bit longer than my original pair - the wires are a bit more robust.

title: An alternative for after Apple breaks your bluetooth...
text:
Anyone who's used iPhones long enough knows this - it's just a matter of time before Apple cranks out a buggy IOS update that causes something on your phone to go wonky, and it may take them quite a while to fix it (if they do). In my case, IOS update 14.7.1 caused my then perfectly working Bluetooth on my phone to pretty much crud out - nothing that uses Bluetooth works properly now, disconnecting regularly, etc. I'm not alone - tons of other comments online from others who have had the same or similar issues after that update. Apple does the usual "really??" bit (they know). Anywayyyyy... I have to use a headset when on the phone, so bought this along with an adapter so that I can plug it into the iPhone's charging port and use it as a wired set since the phone no longer has a plug for this (thanks again, Apple).

Works great, overall. I mean, it doesn't feel like a $100 headset, but then, it doesn't cost that much, too. Microphone arm is adjustable, as is the volume. Gives you enough cord. No cutting off - sound is not perfect but good enough, etc. Shouldn't HAVE to do this because of a phone update, but at least these are here if you need them, and they work. Worth the price.

text:
I've gone through many headphones that I've bought at TJMaxx in an effort not to spend much money on them. They've all broken.

This headset is lasting, and I like having only the one earphone. I don't use this every day though--just once or twice a week for Zoom meetings. But when the meetings are several hours long, I find I don't experience a sore ear, nor does the stabilizer that sits against the skull over the opposite ear begin to irritate. I get terrible migraines from any headset that's too tight or poorly constructed, and so far this headset hasn't triggered one at all.

The sound quality is much better than other headsets I've tried. Now I find myself irritated at people who aren't using headsets, because their sound quality is awful.

It's so easy to swing the microphone up and around and switch to the other ear, if you need a change. The price is incredibly reasonable compared with the money I've spent on other headsets. I'm glad I took the plunge.

title: Revised: Had Problem, Co. Instantly Replaced with New Unit!
text:
I bought the headset in 2019, 9 months ago. The audio seemed weaker than my previous, expensive Rocketfish headset which my parrot broke. Two weeks ago, the mic on this unit failed during a call. I could hear, but no one could hear me. I knew the warranty was up, but decided to see if Wantek would give me credit toward a new one.

I emailed them through Amazon and they instantly offered a new replacement. They shipped it right away and didn't ask for the old unit back. I went for it, and am happier with the replacement. The other party sounds louder, so the unit I had was probably defective from day one.

About this unit: I was happy with the price, and how sturdy this headset is, especially the cord, which is about 1/3 thicker than the more expensive Rocketfish headset I had before. The mike boom is longer, too, and adjusts right over my mouth. It swings away if I'm snacking. :)

The sound quality in the earphone is very good. People say they hear me quite clearly through the mike. I used my phone's "Sound Recorder" function to hear for myself, and the only complaint I had was there was no wind protection. My "Ps" and "Ts" gave wind noise. So, I bought a set of foam "muffs" to put over the mike and voila! It's fine!

I hope to be using this headset for a long time.

title: Great for the price
text:
Overall great value. I don’t use them to drown out sound, but just enough to help me tune out other sounds around me.

As a sleep mask this item works rather well. There is some light leakage for me around the nose, but it cuts out the greater portion of light and doesn’t put pressure on the eyes. Sometimes the padding at the bottom needs adjustment so it’s not pinching my nose. As a side sleeper, I was surprised that the speakers weren’t more uncomfortable. It’s usually a few hours of sleeping on one side before they begin to bother my ears.

I typically only get about 5 to 6 hours of sleep a night and that means I often get two nights worth of play time at about 30% volume. I was actually surprised by the sound quality, I expected it to have a more canned type of sound, but the speakers have a decent range. The speakers do have to be lined up with your ears in order to hear much, but that hasn’t been much of an issue for me.

As to other reviews about things shifting around, I haven’t noticed that with the speakers. You can move the speakers a little bit to adjust them, but I haven’t noticed any big shifts without my input. The controller does move around enough that at times it can be difficult to see the led indicators, but I haven’t had it shift so much that the buttons didn’t work.

title: Adorable colors, smart design (plug slightly shorter?)
text:
The Moshi Moonrock lime color looks very adorable. This obviously doesn't affect the music quality, but it can make them good gift candidates. The headphones are stored in a see-through plastic container that looks like shrink-wrap frustration but you can easily open it with fingers and maybe nails. Two additional ear plug sizes are included (the medium size is installed on the earphones). Also included is a small user manual in many languages. The english part is two pages long. The font is fairly small.

There are three ways to figure out the left/right earphones: 1) the click button is on the right side, 2) the head of the right earphone matches the color scheme (lime in this case) while the head of the left earphone is white 3) a L and R is written next to the point where the audio cable connects to the headphone head.

The sound is as expected in this price range. You are not going to get audiophile quality under $50, but you are also getting better sound than basic headphones included with many devices or you find at the checkout stand in mass market stores.

There are three main areas to cover in this review.

1. Playing music with the 3.5mm cable
Most of the devices I used it with had no problems, but a couple did have problems. The Samsung Chromebook has a known issue with the way its headphone port is designed, so make sure you put the cable all the way in. Initially I didn't realize this, and I could only get audio from the right ear.

The other issue is with the good old Creative Lab Zen mp3 player. Putting the cable all the way in, does not produce good sound. If I leave the cable one step out of the headphone slot, the sound is normal. The Zen was fine with 3 different earphones and two different headphones I tried after noticing this.

This got me looking. An unscientific comparison showed the Moshi plug was very slightly shorter than the other five earphones and headphones.

The majority of devices have no problem. I tried a number of devices after noticing this problem and they had no issues, including the iPod 4 Touch, LG Nexus 4, two older Android phones, original Kindle Fire, Sandisk Clip and Clip Plus mp3 players. Before noticing the problem, I tried it with more devices, but I did not keep track of them since I wasn't expecting this type of an issue to crop up.

2. Click button works with some devices
The Moshi Moonrocks are advertised as Kindle Fire HD headphones, but the Click functionality works with other devices as well in varying degrees. The Play/Pause function works in more devices, but the Next/Previous work with fewer devices.

For example, on the LG Google Nexus 4, all works with the Google Music app. With the Amazon Cloud Player, the previous doesn't work. With the Rdio app, only Play/Pause works. With the YouTube app, play/pause works (I didn't try YouTube playlists, so I don't know if Next/Previous works).

On the iPod 4 Touch with the latest iOS version installed, all four functions work with the Amazon Cloud Player, but only 3 out of 4 with the Rdio app.

It did not work with: first generation Kindle Fire with the native Amazon Music app, Samsung Chromebook, Honeycomb hardware Acer Android tablet, older Android 2.x phone

3. Wrapping the cables
The contraption for wrapping the cables is actually a smart idea but it takes some getting used to it and practice. Once you figure it out, it's fairly easy to get them in and out. Granted, not as fast as throwing them in a bag :)

To put them in the headphone storage:
a. align the two cables attached to the earphone heads into the Y groove of the base
b. the bottom of the storage inverts downwards like a skirt and stays fairly put
c. with the bottom inverted, wrap the cables around it
d. lift up the bottom

To unwrap the headphones, invert the bottom, and unwrap the cables.

title: Sweet Spot Found.
text:
I have IEM dementia. Spent hundreds if not thousands looking for iphone headsets that work for me. I've had Monsters, Shures, Etymōtics, Audio-Technicas, Sonys, JVCs, multiples of some of these brands and many others.

For exercise you need something that is cheap, lays down a good beat, has low cord noise and stays put in your ears. Because you are going to beat on them. I like Nixon Micro Blaster phones. I can find them on eBay for around $16 shipped. Their over-ear cords keep the noise down and stay put. Sound is great for something so cheap.

For airline travel, train commuting, or lawn mowing/snow blowing, you need seriously damped sound isolation. I like Etymōtic's HF3 for these times. They feature a truly fine sounding single balanced armature design and hands down the best microphone in the Apple headphone industry. And their true deep insertion design allows real near total physical sound isolation. Not for use when you need awareness of stuff going on around you.

For compromise use in just about any situation, I have preferred Sony's XBA1i single balanced Armature model, which is now discontinued but can still be found NOS for under $30. A very fine inexpensive headset with refined sound and light compact design. Lacking in deep bass like the Etymōtic but sounds just beautiful anyway.

I have left the Sonys home for these new Senns. The Momentum in-ears have surprisingly balanced frequency response for a dynamic design. Fast and engaging midrange and acceptable highs. Best sounding dynamic IEM I have, better than my much-loved metal bodied JVC Micro HD Carbon Nanotube Japan imports.

And very solid bass without overplaying it like those ridiculously tuned Beats. I have some very expensive 4-driver Sony balanced armature phones and these sound as good in most aspects for a third of the price. Sony's hybrid BA/dynamic designs deliver more engaging sound but boy do you pay for it and they're HUGE. Ditto JVC's multi-driver dynamics.

What Sennheiser has done in this $100 package is deliver a headset that sounds wonderful and is an acceptable compromise of the virtues discussed above such that if you only want to own one pair of headphones this Momentum IEM is a strong contender. Excellent small size, comfortable shape,decent shallow-insertion isolation, beautiful sound with great bass, good cable, mic and remote, durable construction.

All for the market sweet spot price of a hundred bucks and worth every penny.

Some aftermarket Comply-type foam tips can improve isolation still further if you wish, and there are triple flange insertion tips out there that will turn these guys into true isolation stars. I don't like either of those options and find the included silicone tips to work great.

In short, these are great, bone stock right out of the box. If you are so interested that you are reading customer reviews, consider this a full-throated endorsement from a true IEM junkie.

My new all-around favorite. The Sony single BA is relegated to listening in bed. I still recommend it, but these have real bass, stay put better, are far better built and more comfortable.

Total win. Best IEM I've ever tried from Sennheiser.

title: Perfect for Use with an iPhone!
text:
When I talk to my friends for hours on end the last thing I want to do is hold my iPhone in my hand up to my ear or even be on speaker phone. My husband does not like hearing the speaker phone when he's trying to concentrate on his iPhone. It takes too much effort to talk on a speaker phone for hours. So as soon as I answer the phone I switch over to these headphones and talk through the microphone in the headphones. Perfect!

My friend who calls me once a week sounds like a radio DJ, in fact he used to be one but the headphones make him sound that way just naturally. It is really cute. He's always had a nice voice but this makes him come through like rich stereo sound. At first I thought I was talking to a stranger, but got used to his new voice sound.

You just have to hold the button down for a few seconds and an AI voice tells you what the headphones are doing. So if you are finished with the headset you just press the middle button and it tells you the headset is off. So that saves on battery power and makes it easy to know when the power is on or off. I find that I can make these the best volume easily and have it now where I don't need to change it at all.

My friend who calls me every week told me about these headphones and I bought them on his recommendation. I had these years before I got an iPhone because I prepare ahead of time!!!! Now that I have a new iPhone 14 I'm happy as can be with my headset. Since the microphone is built in this is perfect for phone calls but it also works like a regular headphone if you want to listen to audio on your phone. I haven't started listening to music on it yet but will report back when I do. The sound is just superior to any headphones besides my AKG K553s.

~The Rebecca Review

title: Best single-ear set out there
text:
Been through a LOT of bluetooth earpieces in the last couple years. I finally spent the $ for the updated version of my old favorite Voyager...and was it ever worth it.

Battery life is pretty good - not as long as some out there, but with the charging case, it's not a problem. The case is a little oddly shaped, but I do like the dual indicators (for the earpiece and the case battery). The opening at the top with the second set of contacts was puzzling at first, but I suppose you could leave the case plugged in, sitting on you desk and then just set the earpiece into it. I prefer to just close it up inside each time.

Sound quality is great and even standing in the wind, friends could hear me just fine. Most were not even sure I was on a bluetooth earpiece.

I don't listen to music on this much, mostly podcasts on the way to work in the morning, so a single ear is just fine for me. I also like the fact that I can still hear traffic around me.

The flat-ish ear pieces are a little odd and don't feel very secure, but they haven't slipped at all and after a few weeks you don't notice anymore.

One piece of advice - use the original ear tips. I spent $15 on some rounder silicone ones, but they are larger than the largest Plantetonics tips and don't fit in the charging case. If you don't enclose the headset, but just set it in the top charger, then that's probably not an issue though.

I'm not going back to any other earpiece again!

title: Nearly Great
text:
There's a lot to like here, but ultimately it was uncomfortable enough for me to send it back. I'm comparing this with the SteelSeries Arctis 9X. The sound quality and direction are great in both headsets.

Some differences which were important to me:

The Good:
The Stealth uses USB-C. The Arctis uses micro USB.
The Stealth uses a rigid mic boom and swings up out of the way to mute. The Arctis uses a flexible wire boom and has a button (and a red LED indicator when muted) to mute.
There is an iOS app which lets you manipulate settings and such.
Updating the firmware on my Mac was easy.
I experienced only slight connection issues during gameplay compared with the Arctis.

The Bad:
The band across the top is quite firm and after a ~2 hour session was uncomfortable.
The ear cups press in on my head to a level which caused sharp pain towards the end of a ~2 hour sesson.
The Arctis has no iOS app, and the Mac app does not support the latest OS.

Ultimately I kept the Arctis, because the Stealth's were actually painful to use. If they had been more comfortable they beat out the Arctis, IMHO, in every other way.

title: Honest Review
text:
Update - 3/26/22: Right side just went out on me at the worst time. What good is all the high quality material when the driver goes out on you after a few months? I'll give it a couple stars for the experience it gave me, but not a fan of now unexpectedly having to get earbuds again for no good reason.

Original Review: Honestly I don't know what the raving over these is about. Yes they seem very high quality with their braided cord and their heavy drivers, and they are just a TAD bit better sound quality and noise cancelling than the (very) cheap JVC earbuds they replaced. For the price these are a big cut above anything else and I'd recommend them for that alone.

They sent a nice felt pouch to keep them in (who uses these?) and a nice note saying thanks. I appreciated that.

I can't find where the manufacturer is (threw the packaging away before I wrote this, too) but I did read an German address on the packaging, so it's possible it could be a German designed and manufactured product (a big, big plus for quality if so).

Here's the critical part. Maybe I don't have a good enough sound card on my computer (laptop) or phone (S7) to experience the "driving bass" as advertised, but it's nothing special from what I've experienced so far. And with that I don't see why the drivers are that much heavier than normal earbuds. Again, don't get me wrong, the sound quality is pretty good.

What I really bought these for is to replace the cheap earbuds that went out on me all of a sudden, and the mic which I don't have at all. And while they did their job in replacing the earbuds, the mic isn't that good. It works well enough to do the job if you're in a pinch, but it could have been much, much better than it is given the rest of the effort that went into this product.

So all that being said if you're looking for pretty good sound and quality for a cheap price these are it. If you are looking for a cheap set to use the mic with, I'd look elsewhere.

Edit: After getting used to these I had to upgrade the rating to 5 stars, despite how I still feel about the mic. These heavy, corded earbuds are constantly reminding me I got more than I paid for, and after listening to them a while bass does jump out at me in subtle ways. They could probably handle a lot more than what my computer is giving me.

Something that has been a great relief to me as well is they don't get tangled and twisted. Half the time the buds are stuck together when I pick them up to put them on because their magnets are so strong. That probably helps in staying untangled.

title: Not A Good Fit For Me
text:
I’ve been using the 1MORE Stylish True Wireless Earbuds for almost 4 months now (July 2019). Based on the video reviews I watched, I really thought I’d like them. Unfortunately my experience has not been the same as most of the reviewers. The volume is not an issue for me. I do not need to blast my music or podcasts. The battery life has been good enough for what I use them for (cutting the lawn, listen to podcasts while the wife watches her programs on TV). The charging case is great when traveling. The big problem I have is w/the fit. I cannot get the earbuds to fit properly & seal correctly in my ears. I have tried all possible combinations of the ear pieces in the box. Because of this, there is no noise cancellation. Besides the mower being heard loudly, I can hear the television when my wife watches it. If I put in my wired Sony earbuds or my Phaiser BHS-730 BT earbuds, I cannot hear the television over what I’m listening to. The 1MORE earbuds also fall out when I’m moving around. When mowing the lawn, they’ll fall out multiple times.
From my experience, I cannot fully recommend the 1MORE Stylish True Wireless Earbuds. I’d suggest you try to find a pair & see if they fit your ears first. If not, be sure you can return them if they do not fit correctly.

title: The clear best buy for audiophile sound quality & battery life
text: If something approaching audiophile quality sound  is critical (or you primary reason for purchase), the 1More Stylish True Wireless earbuds are a best buy.  You have to spend 3 times the price (for the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless) to get earbuds that sound as good or better than the 1More Stylish.  Period.  Nothing else on the market even comes close.  Treble is crisp and bright.  Mid range sounds are smooth and rendered with nuance.  Bass is true and tight.  And the 1More Stylish battery life is impressive (and far better than that of the Sennheiser Momentum).  Audio talk quality is also quite good - no noise cancellation - but not quite as good as recognized top performers such as the Apple and Sony.  People on the other end of the conversation have told me my voice comes through clear and undistorted. There are a few things that could stand some improvement, however.  First and foremost is fit.  These tend to fall out of my ear; changing to the largest eartips helped, but I still need to be a bit more careful than I think I should need to be.  Secondly, some level of water-resistance would be nice; currently there is no IPX rating at all so these may not be the best choice for wear while exercising.  Third, I would like the controls to be easier to engage.  Lastly, the manual needs a complete overhaul; the print is so small and the ink color/saturation so light that it is unreadable.  All in all, however, these earbuds can't be beat at their price point (approximately $100).

title: Solid $100 TWS, just not for my use case
text:
INTRO:
Been looking for TWS earbuds for a bit now, since I've been tired of having to untangle and fumble with my current IEMs' cable multiple times everyday. They sound good enough for my use of mostly podcasts when I'm on the go and music for when I'm studying, but most importantly they're comfortable and isolate around 7-8/10. I've gotten a $50 budget pair, these, and a $130 pair so far (will have reviews for all of them). Looking for the aforementioned comfort, good isolation, and sound that doesn't noticeably offend.

SOUND:
Probably the best out of the bunch, fun punchy bass was all I really noticed on first listen. Didn't care to really sit down and analyze these like I would headphones or IEMs that I use at home. Most wireless earbuds I've tried so far have a background hissing that I really really dislike, but these didn't. To be expected of a company that actually does well for itself as a low to midrange budget company.

FIT/SEAL:
I used my own single/triple flange eartips. Obviously triple flanges isolate the best, but they were a bit uncomfortable in ear (these are comfortable on my daily drivers) and you won't be able to charge the buds without taking them off. Most of my single flanges fitted on about the same, but also didn't isolate that well. Like a 7/10 at some frequencies, and a 4-5/10 with almost all other noise. The "wings" worked sometimes but would pop out every so often. They didn't make the earbuds unstable in my ears, but simply didn't add to the experience.

LOOKS:
I don't like when the body of an earbud sticks out unnaturally, but these look very natural, reminiscent of the old bluetooth earpieces that I would see businessmen walking around with. However I think this is where the lack of isolation comes from, because only the eartips are working on isolating outside noise.

CHARGING/BATTERY-LIFE:
I used these for a few days and they were at low battery (<30 minutes) because I presumed that they were at least ~50% charged (my mistake here). Case is plastic but still looks nice, and the buds just click in magnetically. Charge time is listed as 85 minutes, but I didn't keep track of it because I don't think I'd ever use these for 6 hours straight, and I always have classes that are ~80 minutes or more where I can just leave these charging if I wasn't managing the battery life well. After a full day of listening I got a "medium battery life" left. (The earbuds will tell you how much battery life is left, but I was also able to see a small bar next to the bluetooth symbol on my phone that gave me a relative sense of where my battery was at) So that was roughly 3-4 hours of listening.

CALLS:
I don't get calls too often, but it is nice to have the option to quickly take a call by pressing once on the button on top of the bud. Sound quality according to my friend was decent enough, but picks up background noise (obviously shouldn't expect too much from something that has to sit on your ears and pick up your voice).

BUTTON:
The button is nice for play/pause, but sadly doesn't have an assistant feature (the $40 buds did). I found myself accidentally pushing it during the first day when I was trying to adjust the fit and insertion of the tips. The button is nice and tactile, without requiring too much force. Location is good because you can use it with 2 fingers to get a solid push without moving the buds much at all (a problem I had with the $130 option).

VERDICT: Won't be keeping, but had a lot of promising high quality pieces that would make this great for someone that wants to hear the environment around them. title: Finally! Great sounding earbuds that stay put!
text:
I've reviewed more than a few sets of earbuds for Amazon through their Vine program. Some were quite inexpensive, some, not so much. My chief complaint with virtually all of them boils down to FIT. The darn things just don't stay lodged in my ear canals. I've even tried using those pricey memory foam ear tips. Those tips help, but then most buds don't fit in the charging case with them in place.

I just purchased these 1More Stylish earbuds and am really pleased with them. I was attracted to them for their claim that they would fit and stay fit... and they're close to perfect for me. I've not even changed the tips that came with them out of the box and have used them for several hours. Only occasionally do they feel like they will come out and a gentle push re-secures them. Only once did one fall out unexpectedly while I was on a long walk. For me, this is remarkable, almost a world record.

How do they sound? Great - the highs are high, the lows are low without being forced. Podcasts sound natural and music is a joy. I listen to an eclectic mix of jazz, classical and 60s & 70s rock and it all sounds great. I read several reviews about these and only one complained that they distorted the bass frequencies. Not in my ears - if anything, they put the bass track back where they belong - in the background, well balanced and appropriate, but not predominant. There is no noise cancellation working here other than the tight fit that blocks out exterior sounds.

My best earbuds for sound prior to these 1Mores were the Jabra 65T.... they were natural and well-balanced, but wouldn't stay in my ears for more than a couple of minutes. You should have seen me crawling under my seat in coach on a trip to London, trying to retrieve the earbud that rolled under me - in the dark. Nice sound, but who cares if you can't wear them? These 1Mores are at least as great-sounding as those Jabras at a much better price.

Complaints? Sure - they're not perfect - I know of no earbuds that have zero weaknesses. Here's my short list:

- Case: it's a bit large, considering the size of the buds themselves. You're not going to slide these into your jeans unless you wear those jeans really loose.

-Charging: there is no indicator telling you the charge level of the case, itself. When you take the buds out of the case, you get this cool "1More" music jingle, then a message telling you the charge level ("Battery High".) Fine - the buds get charged every time you use them and put them back into the case. But there's no way to tell you that the case is getting close to empty until you take the buds out and get a message other than "Battery High." Now, these are $100 earbuds, so I don't expect frills and lace, but some sub-$30 earbuds have charge level indicators on their case.

- Manual: skimpy at best, there's no troubleshooting information and their website needs a major upgrade to be supportive. The manual is awful - light grey letters of the tiniest font printed on glossy paper. Bring your own magnifying glass, 'cuz you're gonna need it

- Support: not terribly responsive. I read that there was a firmware update and downloaded the app from the Google Play Store. I ran it and lost all the sound in one channel - whichever one connected to blue tooth last. I reached out to 1More support a couple of times. I called them and got the ever-popular "COVAD19 excuse" for not being available. It took them a couple of days to get back to me, but their email solved my issue.

Wrap-up
I really like these. The sound is really good for me - on a par with the really expensive Jabras I had but sold on Ebay. (Damn things just wouldn't stay in my ears!) They're not overly large and don't make me look like a freak when I wear them.

title: Great headset, even better deal!
text:
*This is a first thoughts review. There will be an update posted if there is any damage similar to the black headset also shown in the images*

I received them yesterday. They were on sale with -$50 to the $149.99 MSRP. These headphones are awesome! However, you can only gain access to ldac through a firmware update that is done through the app. I had to do 2 updates total.

Q30's vs. Q45's:

Sound quality: points to Q45
Q45 has ldac while q30 does not. They have a similar sound signature, but both can be customized. My favorite sound signature comes from the q30's set to "acoustic" on the Soundcore app. This audio signature is achieved on the Q45's by the screenshots included. #1 is strictly the Soundcore app. #2 is for devices with a 10 band or higher EQ. With my testing, the Q45 is closer to neutral with the stock EQ, but it can be improved greatly with that 10 band EQ. If your phone does not have Dolby Atmos or if that EQ is still not present, "Flat Equalizer - Bass Booster" on the play store has a 10 band EQ. You can also use a 10 band EQ on windows if your PC or laptop has the latest realtek audio console software.

Comfort: toss up
The Q45's have better ear muffs, being larger in diameter and thicker, and more comfortable. The q30's have a better padding for your head, however, it is not that big of a deal if you have your headset adjusted correctly.

Build quality: points to Q45
The Q45's had a sturdier build than the q30's which cracked and broke above the adjustment sliders.

ANC: Points to Q45
The Q45 has better noise cVancelling in general. Not only does it stop more noise, but the app lets you customize your ANC further. With the Q30'S, you get to switch between 3 different presets which vary in effectiveness, but the Q45's allows you to adjust the level of noise it cancels or gives you the option to let Soundcore decide what noise cancelling levels to apply and when. The Q30's microphones are placed at the back of the headset, while the microphones on the Q45's are lower to the bottom of the headset, making for better placement and improving the next topic:

Transparency: toss up
The Q45's have a louder transparency volume, but lack soundstage. It more or less sounds like you cut 2 circular holes in your headset, one in the middle of each ear cup. The Q30's are less loud, but have better sound stage. It does not sound like you have holes cut into your headphones, but rather the headphones sound like they are open back to a certain degree. Despite having better soundstage, the Q30's microphone placement means that wearing the headset correctly makes you hear everything behind you, or everything in front of you if you flip it the other Q4.

Loudness: toss up
They can get just as loud as each other

text:
I had been casually using them around the house just to test them. In this aspect, they're very useful and functional if you are wanting to drown out the background noise. I thought I wouldn't like them because I would get sweaty and hit with them on but I was wrong.

I took them on my first flight since purchasing them. I had other headphones and buds as backup but I didn't need them. I pretty much had them on from boarding until I took them off for landing. They were so comfortable I forgot about any of my concerns. Yes I got a little warm but I didn't sweat nearly as much as I thought I might and the sound was good. The most impressive thing for me was the noise canceling. It drowned our all noise to the point where I barely even noticed it anymore. I did have to turn up the volume a bit but with other headphones, I've had to max out the volume to get the output needed so I could hear the movie. This pair didn't need that.

It was quite the difference when I switched modes with a single button press and transparency mode basically let me hear things as they were. A little muffled but what a difference between that and noise cancelling.

These are coming with me everywhere I travel now. No question.

text: Soundcore by Anker Space Q45 headphones rival the top-rated Sony WH-1000XM4 and Bose QuietComfort 45 at 1/3 of the price. I actually own both the Q45 and Q20. I used the Q45 at night to get a good night sleep because my wife snored too much. I've bought the highly rated and expensive QuietOn 3.1 noise cancelling earphones but after trying them, I've found that they did reduce the volume of my wife's snoring by about 2/3 but I could still heard a quieter but disruptive snoring! The Q45's noise cancellation was actually very good thanks to the hybrid and active noise cancelling functions. However, due to EMF concern because having a Bluetooth transmitter next to my head for a long time may not be good even though the radiation level is low, I only used the direct 3.5mm cable connection to turn off the Bluetooth transmission and only used the ANC. This can only be done with the Q45, not Q20. I used the latter one with Bluetooth on for workout because the Bluetooth duration is only for a short period of time so I think it's OK. I found the Q45 was the best choice because of 3 things: 1) Noise Isolation 2) ANC 3) The ability to play pink noise from an external device. The QuietOn 3.1 lacks the last function! I played a falling rain to drowned out the weaker snoring sound that the ANC could completely remove and that put me through a good night sleep through a pleasant falling rain :-)

title: Excellent Sound from Great Fitting Smaller Size TWS BT5 Earbuds w/ Charging Case, Rose Gold Color
text:
I love listening to music and really enjoy a great pair of ear phones to use when I walk, work around the house or read. Picture 1 shows the full set which I received with 6 extra pair of silicone eartips (deep and 1/2 height) and a USB A to C cable to charge the case. I loved the smaller size and additional eartips of this set of TWS Bluetooth 5 earbuds that are also IPX-7 Waterproof. That's better than most! These look great too.

I found using the Bluetooth 5.0 pairing connection easy to make with either my phone or iPod device. Range was as good as any without dropping out over a room away. I experienced no trouble and if the connection dropped due to distance, reconnection was automatic. These use touch controls on each earbud with a Bass Boost Mode on the Right bud (3 presses gives 2 Beeps for ON,One for OFF), a No Lag Movie Mode (4 Presses on either) and the usual volume & pause controls as well as "Voice Assistant". They were very responsive to my touch. I loved the control choices that are clearly explained on the box.

These sound crisp and clean with great mids, vocals and high end sound and excellent boosted bass. Way better sound than some buds over twice this price! Vocal tones sounded great too. I loved how they sounded and when being used with my phone and callers found my voice quality very good from the built in microphones. The sound drivers are very well tuned and give good low end sound without boost; these are not skull thumping boomers but do quite well. Even turned down very low they were good. I really liked how these sounded which is ultimately what a great pair of ear buds is all about. The comfortable fit helps also.

The instructions warn not to use more than a 5V 1A USB charging source for the case. Quote" Do not use a charger that exceeds 5V 1A. A higher powered charger may damage the battery." I did not like that as I have quite a few higher powered chargers and it is easy to use one that may damage this case. That would drop a half star but since there are no halves, I'll default to 5. They do indicate that the case won't overcharge if left plugged in, so that's good...so long as it's not a high powered charger!

I Highly Recommend these Tempo 30 Rose Gold Wireless Earbuds for Small Ears Women, Cute Pink Bluetooth Bass Boost Earphones Small Ear Canals, IPX7 Sweatproof, 32-Hour Long Battery. I think these are superb for the price and these sound excellent to me!

I hope you’ve found the information and my review helpful.

title: A good value
text: I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don’t seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn’t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That’s really my only complaint - there’s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

title: Great Noise Cancelling Headphones
text:
My work bought each person in my branch a pair of QC25’s from Amazon. I also own a set of QC2’s.

I have to say, whether I’m wearing my QC25’s or QC2’s, I love my Bose QC headsets and will not travel without them. I also use them for work, not just at work.

Since I have both a pair of the old and new, I thought I’d do my own comparison:

1. Equally comfortable

2. In a quiet environment, where noise cancelling isn’t really a factor, I think the sound quality (even of the older QC2’s) is pretty comparable. If I were thinking about upgrading just for sound quality, I don’t think I would.

3. Noise cancelling has definitely improved in the QC25’s over the older QC2’s. In a noisey environment where noise cancelling matters, the difference is noticeable. The QC2’s are good, the QC25’s are clearly better.

4. The QC25’s will work w/o a battery. If the battery dies in the QC25, you will have music, just not NC. In the older QC2’s, the headphones would not work at all w/a dead or no battery.

5. QC25’s have a mic for taking or making phone calls. The QC2’s did not.

6. The case is smaller, but just as protective for the QC25’s. The QC2’s do not fold up as small.

7. They both look good.

8. The prices really haven’t changed over the years.

The bottom line, I love my Bose headsets, both of them. I would absolutely recommend buying a set, particularly if you have a need for a set of quality headphones at work or for travel.

For me, after reviewing the older and newer QC headsets, I don’t think I’d upgrade until the older QC2’s stopped working. I think that Bose headsets are built so well, that time doesn’t diminish the quality and utility of Bose’s older products.

title: Isolate your ears and light up your mind
text:
Upgraded to the QC25 from the very popular ~$35 Sony noise cancelling headset that you can find on Amazon. The difference is spectacular, which is very welcome considering the "slight" difference in price. An amazing piece of technology that is of exceptional sturdiness and quality. I got the Samsung version and the in-line cable controls work perfectly for my Galaxy S6 Edge.

On to the actual quality of the main feature. The leather ear covers are soft, sweat/oil repellent, and don't leave any marks on my skin afterwards. The inside of the ear cups are slightly curved, I'm assuming so that the sound is project more directly into your ear. I have quite large, protruding ears and these fit perfectly. The noise cancelling feature is outstanding - I am sitting next to an aquarium with multiple fans, pumps and filters on and if I was blindfolded I wouldn't be able to tell you if I was in my room or in the middle of a park. Sound quality is the best of any headphone I've ever used, leagues above any stock earbuds. You will hear the individual piano keys being struck in a classical piece, and the subtle breathing inflections of a singer.

title: UPDATE: Failed 12 days after the 1-year warranty ended. Not worth the high cost
text:
I was using the ModMic 4.0 with my Sennheiser HD800 headphones. Gaming headsets always sound like trash so I was happy that the ModMic gave me good microphone audio without having to compromise headphone quality. The cable was so annoying though. It was rigid and would always get caught under my office chair or tangled with my legs and/or headphone cable. The ModMic Wireless solves those problems.

PROS:
-It's wireless. This is the only reason I made the purchase. The cord was really annoying
-The mic can be switched between omni and uni-directional. I found that omni-directional sounded better for me.
-Uses same magnet mount as the wired version. The sticky pads on the magnet mounts aren't great and replacements are way overpriced so I had to superglue mine to my HD800's when it fell off. For this reason I'm SO glad the mounts are the same and I don't have to pry off the superglued magnet.

CONS:
-My gaming friends said it doesn't sound as good as the wired version in discord.
-Sticky pads on the magnet mount are weak. Had to superglue it to my headphones after it fell off.
-Price. It costs more than twice as much as my wired ModMic. Seems a bit steep
-You have to have install it on the right side so the charging port faces down if you want to be able to use it while charging with the included USB cable. I hate the mic on the right side so I will never be able to use it cabled/charging.

UPDATE: -1 more star because the battery life is poor. I have had so many times where I'll be talking in discord and nobody is responding because the microphone died. The 12 hour battery life claim is not true. I get about half of that.

NEW UPDATE: 12 days after the 1-year warranty ran out it started having pairing problems. It would disconnect and become unpaired. Re-pairing would only last seconds to minutes before it would stop pairing again. For the high cost, it shouldn't have failed so quickly. Also the quickly diminishing battery life was a big downside.

title: Essential device to free you to chose better headphones
text:
I don't know what it is, but as soon as companies add a mic boom to their headsets, the audio quality of the headphones seems to drop off, but the price doesn't.
This wireless mic lets you turn any headphones or VR headset into one with a mic boom. And when it comes time to get new cans, you can just slap this mic on the new ones!

If you use VR and you have anything other than an Index (which has a very good mic), this is a game-changer. I've used all of the major HMDs, and they all have atrocious microphones, save for the Index. That isn't a big deal unless you are into social games, or like to stream.

The only feature I wish we could get is sidetone (hearing yourself). It's easier to speak when you can hear yourself, especially when using headsets that isolate outside sound. But I can't think of any way they could do this, so I'm not counting it against them. The delay on this mic is minimal enough to not affect your experience, but it would be distracting if you enabled software sidetone.

All in all, highly recommended for:
-VR HMDs
-Any good pair of headphones
-Use for semi-pro voice recording. Quality is great but you'll want sidetone for very serious work
-Any VOIP gaming needs
-Voice dictation. The positioning and sound isolation make this a great microphone for voice to text

Pros:
-Higher quality audio than expected, considering it is wireless
-Easy to install and use. Plug it in, slap on a magnet and you're off

-Reasonably priced!

title: Skullcandy INK'D vs. JVC Marshmallow . . . which one comes out ahead?
text:
When it comes to in-ear, noise blocking type earphones, I had been using JVC Marshmallows for a couple of years, but since these Skullcandy INK'D earphones were less expensive, are extremely popular, and pretty highly rated, I decided to give them a try.

A major difference is that the Skull candy ear bud is made of pliable material (probably silicone rubber), while the Marshmallow buds are made of hard sponge. Skullcandy provides three different sizes of buds, so hopefully you will get a nice fit. The middle sized one fit me the best, and when inserted in the ear, I can very quickly and easily get a nice tight, sealed fit, that blocks most ambient noise. The sound quality is very good, for music, with good bass response, and room for the music to resonate. The earphones are also good for podcasts or audio books, where the midtones of voices sounds nice and full.

Noise blocking earphones, with earbuds that seal in the ear canal, usually have the 'stethoscope effect'. This involves the transmission of sound, through the wires, and into the ear. The sound is similar to tapping a live microphone, a muffled bumping sound, which can be very irritating. Sound is transmitted amazing well through the cable and the soft Skullcandy earbuds. So if you are doing something where you are moving around and bumping the cord, or have clothing rubbing against the cord, some annoying sounds will most likely be transmitted into the ear. A really strong wind can also transmit sound. This problem is not as pronounced with the JVC phones.

Long term, the hard sponge JVC buds will probably outlast the silicone ones on the INK'D's. In addition, JVC also provides a spare set of buds, so for durability, JVC comes out ahead. For comfort though, the Skullcandy phones might have the edge. They may not block out as much noise, and may transmit some unwanted sounds, but they seem lighter and don't need to be adjusted as much to get a good fit.

The earphones are in the same price range, and both provide good performance, come in a variety of colors, and have a straight pin jack, instead of an L shaped one, which is generally less prone to breakage. If you really want to block out ambient sound, the JVC does a better job. If you prefer a little more comfort, and can live with some possible noise, the Skullcandy may work well. For the INK'D earphones, typically at Amazon, there is usually one color that is cheaper than the others, so if you wait a while the color you prefer may eventually be the one that is on sale.

title: Amazing value. Great sound quality, and great features.
text:
These are great earbuds - especially for the price. They're comfortable, and the silicone tips do a great job of noise isolation. The touch controls are easy and intuitive. I like the convenience of wireless and USB-C charging, and the stated battery life is 8 hours for music. Also, I found they held up a lot better at the edge of Bluetooth range than others I own.

The charging case is portable - easy to fit into a pocket or purse for sure. But most importantly, the earbuds seat easily and securely in the case, which I've found to be an issue in other similar products I've tried in the past. So no phantom connections or finding the earbuds didn't actually charge.

Overall, I'd definitely recommend these. I actually haven't found anything I dislike about them - which is rare for me.

title: Good for calls, music not so much
text:
I am comparing these to Tozo T6.
Pros:
-Call quality is so much better than T6. Probably because of the location of the mic.
-The controls are pretty much the same as T6 & easy to access.
-Fit Is decent...right earbud kind of hurt my ear. Could be my ear could be the bud. I can't get T6 to stay in my ears for any significant length of time.

Cons:
-No beep or sound when you hang up a call so I always have to look and see if the call ended.
-Music quality in my opinion is poor. Between T6 and T9, T6 has noticeably superior sound.

It's not bad for a pair of inexpensive earbuds. They go on sale often for under $30. I am debating whether to return them or not since the call quality is so good. But the music quality just isn't doing it for me. That's the trade off.

title: The sound is on point.. The ease of use, is amazing!
text:
Before reading, small caveat- Im a 40+ yr. old mom that loves my 80’s tunes.. Freddie Mercury, Boy George, Go-Go’s.. Wham! Ho-Jo and Frankie goes to Hollywood!!! These bands transcend me to a younger/carefree time in life ..A time in life of quality music!!! Well, If you can believe it.. my astute taste in music is not shared amongst my teenage and college kids. So, when traveling as a family unit, I have been deemed the outcast… and my music is reserved for only finest tastes- translation: I must listen ALONE in my own device!!

I am not a music connoisseur or some techno guru therefore, when I plug in a headset- (notice I said plug in.. Bluetooth makes me crazy!! I like control over everything and not being tech savvy means, I would need the help to hook me up... NoT!)

when listening to music, I expect some standard of quality. No sound distortion- residual vibration from base- and results to produce crisp sounding vocals. When this happens I consider it a success…PALOVUE LIGHTENING HEADPHONES was the trifecta of all my requirements- I was pleasantly surprised a basic/minimal plug-in headphone set could bring a decent of quality sound at such a reasonable price. Again- not a connoisseur… don’t hold me to the verbiage that, i wouldn’t know if I tried to review on a more technical level..!!

I realize, I may be the only one that truly believes the greatest invention was the Sony Walkman..??! me/my cassettes back in the 80’s had a beautiful love affair!! (OMG-saving babysitting $ for batteries was my life..!!) Obviously, this headset surpasses that level in comparison.. Yet, I have the same feeling of being in a happy Bliss!!!

I will add, our house boasts 2 pairs of AirPods, a pair of beats, and one Skullcandy high quality lightening platinum headset... I’ve tried them all! I don’t have a complaint about them, other than… OMG- The dang price! Summer jobs, Santa Claus and the likes have been too good to allow my children these luxuries but, that is just what those are LUXURIES!! For my purpose of listening to music at the pool, taking a brisk walk or, traveling with the fam… these are perfect! Best of all- I won’t cry or, die.. IF, something happened and these stopped working or, heaven forbid became lost!

These are simple, straightforward, easy to use from the moment removed from package!! This set is free of needing help to pair with Bluetooth as, you just plug-in to device.. and go- BooM!! These have standard 3 size ear cushions, to help find a good fit. BUT, the added bonus I appreciated was the clip, its super handy... it allows headphones to be attached to ones shirt- alleviating any excess pull or tension on the slack of the wires. Basically, it helps so, weight of the product will not to pull down on itself- making headphones pop out of ears...
These would be a great product for someone younger/older that like things simple.. or, lack text savvy skills and must have simple hook up. I myself struggle with Bluetooth connections and my ego takes a hit asking over and over for help in this department.. so, I relate. (I’m thinking this would be a perfect gift for my grandma- she could connect to her cellphone device -as grandma takes a walk each morning at the ripe old age of 86! This would be a great gift in the future- just plug in connection, and have her Dolly Parton tunes as she heads out on her walk!) This pair of headphones could be compatible for a variety of people..
